problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate budget across 14 infrastructure projects to maximize the overall community benefit score.  
The characteristics of each project are:  
* Project A: benefit score 0.124, impact index 0.162, allocation limits [0.053, 0.675]  
* Project B: benefit score 0.188, impact index 0.212, allocation limits [0.100, 0.371]  
* Project C: benefit score 0.037, impact index 0.187, allocation limits [0.035, 0.809]  
* Project D: benefit score 0.074, impact index 0.042, allocation limits [0.013, 0.780]  
* Project E: benefit score 0.086, impact index 0.222, allocation limits [0.056, 0.899]  
* Project F: benefit score 0.088, impact index 0.192, allocation limits [0.052, 0.548]  
* Project G: benefit score 0.032, impact index 0.296, allocation limits [0.063, 0.500]  
* Project H: benefit score 0.097, impact index 0.150, allocation limits [0.049, 0.636]  
* Project I: benefit score 0.119, impact index 0.210, allocation limits [0.018, 0.683]  
* Project J: benefit score 0.073, impact index 0.281, allocation limits [0.061, 0.307]  
* Project K: benefit score 0.044, impact index 0.296, allocation limits [0.071, 0.421]  
* Project L: benefit score 0.145, impact index 0.093, allocation limits [0.098, 0.469]  
* Project M: benefit score 0.069, impact index 0.187, allocation limits [0.000, 0.774]  
* Project N: benefit score 0.115, impact index 0.102, allocation limits [0.002, 0.485]  

Each project must receive a budget share within its specified limits, and all shares must sum to 1. To ensure timely completion, the group of high-priority projects L = {A, C, D, F, G, H, I, K, L, M, N} must collectively receive at least 0.455 of the total budget. Additionally, the overall impact index of the portfolio must not exceed 0.248, and the total benefit score must be at least 0.083. Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
